_synthetic: SYNTHETIC COVERAGE SAMPLE. Blank government form, invented taxpayer. Every value is an obvious placeholder (Testcorp, 000-00-0000, 555-01xx). No real PII. Its job is to exercise every MAPPED path in 433aoi.map.json map_version 2 - printed page 1 (Sections 1 and 2) and printed page 2 (Section 3 lines (1a) through (4)) - and nothing else. Pages 3-8 are not mapped yet and this fixture carries no keys for them.
_coverage_notes: SCOPE. 74 of this form's 425 fields are on page 1; 72 of those are bound and 2 are the never-autofill push buttons. This fixture reaches all 72. The other 351 fields are on pages 2-8 and are deliberately untouched - the read-back is a statement about the slice, not about the form.

EVERY SCALAR NAMES ITSELF. Twenty-six text cells, twenty-six distinct values, each saying which cell it belongs in. That is not decoration: this form declares a /MaxLen on only 13 of its 425 fields and on NONE of the 26 cells here, so cell SIZE proves nothing about which column a value landed in. On 433-A a 5-digit mileage in a 16-char Make/Model column is refused by the field; here the same mistake would print silently. Distinct self-naming values are the only thing that makes a mis-binding visible in the read-back.

MARITAL STATUS IS 'married' SO THE DATE OF MARRIAGE CELL IS COHERENT. s1_date_of_marriage is a mapped text cell and a saturated fixture must reach it; filling it while declaring 'unmarried' would exercise the cell at the cost of printing a contradiction.

HOUSING STATUS IS 'other' FOR THE SAME REASON. s1_housing_other_specify is the specify blank beneath 'Other (specify e.g., share rent, live with relative, etc.)', and it is the one arguable binding in this slice (the caption sits one printed row above the cell rather than beside it, because the 'Other' checkbox occupies the caption's own row). Choosing 'other' here means the read-back shows the specify text printed directly under the box it belongs to, which is the check a person makes by looking.

PAY PERIODS DIFFER ON PURPOSE - taxpayer bi-weekly, spouse monthly. The two sets are four boxes at IDENTICAL x columns, 86 points apart in y, under two captions that read the same word for word ('Pay period'). Identical values would hide a copy/paste between the You[0] and Spouse[0] subforms; different ones do not.

OWNERSHIP INTEREST DIFFERS TOO - taxpayer yes, spouse no. Same reason: the two questions are worded differently on the page but their checkbox pairs are structurally identical, and the Yes box of one sits at the same x as the Yes box of the other.
OPTION VALUES VARY IN CASE AND PADDING (' Married ', 'BI-WEEKLY', a boolean true, a string 'No') to exercise the trim + case-insensitive match rather than assuming every caller normalises first.

s1_community_property_state_last_10_years IS THE FORM'S LONE CHECK-HERE BOX. There is no 'No' cell for it anywhere on the page - the negative answer is the box left blank - so it exercises the `check_here` construct, which 433-A has no use for. It is set true here; a false or absent value is the same printed outcome and would prove nothing.

household_members CARRIES FIVE RECORDS AGAINST FOUR SLOTS. This form prints four dependent rows where 433-A prints five (433-A repeats Row4 under duplicate leaf names). The fifth record exists to prove overflow is LOGGED AND DROPPED rather than thrown or silently written over Row4, and to prove the 4-slot cap is read from the map rather than assumed from 433-A.

EACH DEPENDENT ROW NAMES ITS OWN PRINTED ROW ('Row 1 Dependent' ... 'Row 4 Dependent') and carries a distinct age and relationship. The four rows print at y 324.0, 309.6, 295.2 and 280.8, and the map binds Row1..Row4 in that descending order; identical filler would have hidden a reversal, which is exactly the defect that reached 433-F's account tables.

THE FOUR ROWS ANSWER THE TWO YES/NO PAIRS IN ALL FOUR COMBINATIONS (yes/yes, yes/no, no/yes, no/no). The 'Claimed as a dependent on your Form 1040' pair and the 'Contributes to household income' pair are two separate 9-point boxes 97 points apart on the same printed row; answering every row the same way would leave a swap between the two columns invisible.
AGES ARE FOUR CHARACTERS OR FEWER. The Age column is the only /MaxLen-bearing cell in this slice (/MaxLen 4, x 219.6..248.4). Nothing else on page 1 declares one.

NO SPLIT VALUES. 433-A splits every phone across two abutting /MaxLen-limited cells; this form prints primary phone, secondary phone and FAX as single cells (x 198.0..316.8, no /MaxLen), so the phone numbers here are written whole. If a future revision splits them, this fixture will fail loudly rather than truncate.
_coverage_notes_page_2: SCOPE. 68 of this form's 425 fields are on page 2 and all 68 are bound - page 2 has no IRS-use column, no link button and no cell this slice could not resolve, so it carries no never-autofill and no deferred entries. This fixture reaches all 68. Together with page 1 that is 142 of 425; the other 283 are on pages 3-8 and are deliberately untouched.

EVERY MONEY VALUE ON PAGE 2 IS DISTINCT, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Twenty-six money cells, twenty-six different figures, none of them a round multiple of another except the one pair that is SUPPOSED to be. Page 2 prints six blocks of the shape 'value cell, operator, value cell, = , total cell', all at the same x columns, and none of them declares a /MaxLen. A row swapped with the row below it, or a figure copied from the block above, would print inside the rules and every total would still add up. Only distinct figures make it visible.

THE QUICK SALE TRIPWIRE IS THE REASON 88000 WAS CHOSEN. 3a_retirement_accounts[0].current_value is 88000; the printed 'X .8 = $' cell must therefore read 70400, and 3a is 70400 - 5400 = 65000. If the map had bound that cell by its leaf name Times_7 and multiplied by 0.7, it would read 61600 and 3a would be 56200. Those are 8800 and 8800 apart from the right answers - large, obvious, and NOT reachable by any rounding. A rounder figure like 100000 would give 80000 and 70000, which look equally plausible side by side.

THE FIRST BANK ROW IS 'Cash', WHICH ONLY SLOT 0 CAN BE. Printed line (1a) offers six account types and printed line (1b) offers five - the same list without Cash. Putting Cash on the first row exercises the option that exists on one slot only, which is the whole of the asymmetry the map declares. Its institution and account-number cells say what they are rather than naming a bank, because a Cash row has neither and a saturated fixture still has to reach both cells.

THE THIRD BANK ROW AND THE SECOND RETIREMENT ROW ARE OVERFLOW. The form prints two bank rows and one retirement row; the extra records exist to prove overflow is LOGGED AND DROPPED rather than thrown or written over an earlier row, and to make the point the printed page makes - a dropped row is exactly what (1c) 'Total of bank accounts from attachment' and (3b) 'Total of retirement accounts from attachment' are for. Their figures are NOT in 1c or 3b: those cells are declared not checkable precisely because what they sum is on an attachment this engine never sees.

BOTH INVESTMENT ROWS FILL THE UNLABELLED WRITE-IN, AND THEY DO IT DIFFERENTLY ON PURPOSE. That cell carries no printed caption of its own and the map binds it on x as the 'Other' specify blank, flagged arguable. Slot 0 is typed 'other' so the write-in is coherent under that reading. Slot 1 is typed 'bonds' and its write-in reads as a detail line, which is coherent under the OTHER reading. Filling both ways means this fixture does not assert which reading is right - which is what an arguable binding is entitled to.

TYPE OPTIONS ARE NOT ALL EXERCISED AND THAT IS ACCOUNTED FOR. Page 2 declares 21 checkboxes across three option lists and this record checks six of them - one type per row plus the lone digital asset box. The other fifteen are reported by verify-form-coverage.mjs as 'checkboxes unchecked (independent)', a declared state and not a gap, because no page-2 set is declared exclusive. See the map's exclusive._note_page_2.

OPTION VALUES AGAIN VARY IN CASE AND PADDING ('Money Market Account/CD', ' 401K ', 'Other') to exercise the trim + case-insensitive match, and the multi-word slash-bearing option is chosen deliberately: it is the only option on this page that could be mangled by a naive key comparison.

EVERY ROW STATES ITS asset_class. All four page-2 groups declare row_class, and a row claiming a class its group does not print stops the run. On this form investments (2) carry no multiplier and retirement accounts (3) carry X .8, so a 401(k) filed into the investment table would understate nothing visibly and overstate the offer by 20% of market value. The class is what refuses it.

_coverage_notes_page_3: SCOPE. 59 of this form’s 425 fields are on page 3 and all 59 are bound - page 3 has no IRS-use column, no link button and no cell this slice could not resolve, so it carries no never-autofill and no deferred entries. This fixture reaches all 59. Together with pages 1 and 2 that is 201 of 425; the other 224 are on pages 4-8 and are deliberately untouched.

EVERY FMV ON THE FORM IS DISTINCT, AND SO IS EVERY QUICK SALE VALUE. Page 3 adds four market values - 415000, 187500, 34750, 52375 - against page 2’s 88000, 50000, 31500 and 27300, and the eight quick sale values and equities they produce collide with nothing. Page 3 prints four blocks of the shape ‘value cell, X .8, quick sale cell, minus, loan cell, =, total cell’ at the same x columns with no /MaxLen anywhere, so a figure copied from the block above would print inside the rules and reconcile. Only distinct figures make it visible.

EVERY FMV IS A MULTIPLE OF 5, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. An integer dollar amount times .8 lands on a whole dollar only when the amount is a multiple of 5. The form’s own instruction says to round to the nearest dollar; the tripwires compare exactly to the cent and model no rounding (433aoi.totals.json records that as a known limit). Choosing multiples of 5 means a failing tripwire on this fixture is a real defect and never a rounding artefact.

VEHICLE 1 IS OWNED AND VEHICLE 2 IS LEASED, WHICH IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE PAIR AVAILABLE. The (6a)/(6c) caption reads ‘Total value of vehicle (if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value)’. Vehicle 2 therefore prints 52375 as its market value and 41900 as its quick sale value - the X .8 cell is UNCONDITIONAL and is written on a leased row exactly as on an owned one - and prints 0 at (6c) even though quick sale value minus loan would be 2300. That is what makes the read-back show, on the page, why (6a)/(6c) is declared not checkable while both quick-sale tripwires stay live. A fixture with two owned vehicles would have exercised neither.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT (6d) IS ZERO UNDER BOTH READINGS OF ITS CONDITIONAL, and this is stated rather than hidden. (6d) is max(0, (6c) - 3450) on a joint offer and (6c) unchanged otherwise; with (6c) at 0 both branches give 0. So this fixture does not distinguish the two readings of (6d) - it does not need to, because (6d) is declared not checkable for a reason no fixture can remove: the phrase ‘joint offer’ is drawn exactly once on all eight pages, in that caption, and no cell on this form records the answer.

(6b) IS THE VEHICLE ALLOWANCE AND IT IS EXERCISED ON A REAL NUMBER. 16375 - 3450 = 12925, so the printed constant bites and the floor does not. The floor on this line was proved separately against a fixture whose (6a) was 0. The other printed constant on this form, the -$1,000 at line (1), is exercised by the page-2 figures unchanged.

THE THIRD PROPERTY AND THE THIRD VEHICLE ARE OVERFLOW. The form prints two of each; the extra records exist to prove overflow is LOGGED AND DROPPED rather than thrown or written over an earlier row, matching the third bank row and second retirement row on page 2. Their figures are NOT in (5c) or (6e): those cells are declared not checkable precisely because what they sum is on an attachment this engine never sees.

OPTION VALUES AGAIN VARY IN CASE AND PADDING. The for-sale answer is ‘Yes’, vehicle 1 is ‘Own’ and vehicle 2 is ‘ lease ’ - padded and lower-case - to exercise the trim plus case-insensitive match on a set where getting it wrong would tick the box that zeroes a printed total.

BOTH PAGE-3 GROUPS STATE THEIR asset_class ON EVERY ROW. 5ab_real_property accepts only real_property and 6ac_vehicles only vehicle. Page 3 is where that matters most on this form: the two tables print the same four-cell money row at the same x columns 200 points apart, and a vehicle filed into a property slot would print inside the rules and reconcile every total on the page.

_coverage_notes_page_4: SCOPE. 66 of this form's 425 fields are on page 4 and all 66 are bound - page 4 has no IRS-use column, no link button and no cell this slice could not resolve, so it carries no never-autofill and no deferred entries. This fixture reaches all 66. Together with pages 1, 2 and 3 that is 267 of 425; the other 158 are on pages 5-8 and are deliberately untouched.

SYNTHETIC. Every name, address, EIN, phone number, account number and wallet address on this page is invented. The EINs are not issued, the website resolves nowhere (.invalid), and the wallet address is not a valid address on any chain.

DISTINCT BY ROW AND BY COLUMN. No two money cells on page 4 share a value, and no money cell shares a value with any cell on pages 2 or 3, so a cell written into its neighbour cannot produce a total that still reconciles. (7a) market value 61,500 / QSV 49,200 / loan 7,325 / total 41,875. (7b) 18,750 / 15,000 / 2,140 / 12,860. (7c) 9,245. (7) 52,000. Box A 444,752. (8a) 3,410. (8b) 27,655. (8c) 18,420. (8d) 6,015. (8) 55,500.

THE TWO QUICK-SALE MULTIPLIERS ARE EXACT AND NOT ROUND. 61,500 x .8 = 49,200 and 18,750 x .8 = 15,000. Both were chosen so the product is a whole number: rounding is NOT implemented in this slice, so a fixture whose X .8 produced cents would be testing the tripwire against a question this engine has not been given an answer to yet. The cents evidence for that decision is in the slice-4 report, not in this fixture.

THE $11,980 DEDUCTION IS EXERCISED AND THE FLOOR IS NOT. (7) is 41,875 + 12,860 + 9,245 - 11,980 = 52,000, comfortably positive. The floor declared on (7) does not fire on this fixture, which is stated here rather than left to be inferred: the floor is a claim about the printed page and this fixture does not prove it.

BOX A CROSSES THREE PAGES. 37,912 (p2) + 81,525 (p2) + 77,750 (p2) + 35,850 (p2) + 138,650 (p3) + 21,065 (p3) + 52,000 (p4) = 444,752. It is the only total on this form so far whose operands are not all on one sheet, so it is the only one that would catch a page-3 figure failing to reach a page-4 line.

LINE (8) HAS NO $1,000 DEDUCTION. 3,410 + 27,655 + 18,420 + 6,015 = 55,500 exactly. The personal line (1) on page 2 subtracts $1,000 and this one does not, so the two are deliberately different arithmetic on deliberately different numbers.

BOTH BUSINESS BANK ROWS EXERCISE A DIFFERENT ACCOUNT TYPE, and slot 1 uses Money Market/CD - an option page 2's second bank row does not offer, because (1b) prints five options and (8b) prints six. The value is written with surrounding spaces and mixed case (" Money Market/CD ") to exercise the normalising fold, the same way the page-3 vehicle row writes " lease ".

OVERFLOW IS EXERCISED TWICE. A second valuable item at (7a), which prints one row, and a third business bank account at (8a)/(8b), which prints two. Both must be dropped and logged, never written over an earlier row.

SECTION 4 IS ALL FREE TEXT AND HAS NO TOTAL. Its one money-shaped cell, average gross monthly payroll, is plain input and is declared not checkable. The three checkbox sets are all exercised, and the type-of-business set is answered "Other" so the write-in cell beside it is reached too.
